Webinar | September 3, 2026 Intensification Of Upstream Operations With Dynamic Perfusion Source: Cytiva Fed-batch cultivation remains the standard for monoclonal antibody production, but perfusion offers compelling opportunities to improve product quality, yield, and facility utilization. Its broader adoption, however, has been limited by process complexity and the challenges of maintaining aseptic operations over extended periods. Dynamic perfusion provides a more streamlined path to continuous cell culture by using a fixed volumetric media feed rate to guide cell growth and metabolism over time. This approach eliminates the need for cell bleed and daily adjustments to the perfusion rate, reducing operational demands while retaining the benefits of process intensification. Explore how dynamic perfusion compares with other upstream strategies in productivity, media consumption, and space-time yield, and learn how it can help address common barriers to continuous biomanufacturing. access the Webinar! Webinar | September 1, 2026 Improved Clearance Of Host Cell Proteins After Virus Inactivation Source: Cytiva Post-viral inactivation filtration can do more than remove precipitates. When carefully developed, it may also reduce residual host cell proteins before polishing chromatography, including lipases that can compromise monoclonal antibody stability. Selecting the right filtration approach requires a close look at several competing priorities: impurity clearance, process fluid throughput, and overall cost. See how multiple Seitz filter media with different charge characteristics and an anion exchange membrane were evaluated using two distinct feeds. The findings illustrate how feed properties and media selection can influence filtration performance and help shape a more reliable, scalable purification process. access the Webinar!
